title: Ops + Product Triage Week Playbook
content:
Purpose
This is a compact, operational playbook for the cross-functional triage week we run before the Q2 OKR freeze and the company all-hands. Goal: produce a prioritized set of asks for execs, a short decision ledger for product/ops trade-offs, and an actionable run-of-show for the all-hands.

Quick context
- Timebox: 5 working days (Mon–Fri). Kickoff: Monday 09:30 PT. Final deliverables due: Friday 17:00 PT.
- Primary outcome: single prioritized task list that feeds into the OKR draft and the all-hands 20-min exec update.
- Who should attend: product leads (hosted-api, dedicated, private), eng leads (serving-runtime, infra, sre), ops, growth, a product marketing rep, Exec (drop-in for Wednesday decision checkpoint).

Agenda (day-by-day)
Day 0 (Fri prior) — prep
- Collect backlog slices: top 5 cross-team blockers per team (Ops/Prod/SRE/Console). See linked Jira queries (OPS-4123, PRD-879).
- Circulate current OKR draft (Confluence: Company-Q2-Planning-3652). Ask: 2-minute highlight from each owner.

Day 1 — kickoff + constraint mapping
- 09:30 Kickoff (30m) — Maya to run: scope, timing, decision criteria (impact / risk / effort / alignment).
- 10:30 Breakouts (teams) — map constraints and dependencies (capacity, infra, launch windows). Capture owners and blockers in the spreadsheet (internal).
- Afternoon: Ops run capacity heatmap (SLO/latency/cost sensitivity). Output: 1-page snapshot.

Day 2 — proposal triage
- Morning: teams present 2 prioritized proposals each (10m per team). Focus on proposals that change cost/latency or require infra changes.
- Decision rubric introduced: impact (1–5), customer reach (1–5), cost delta (–3 to +3), ramp risk (1–5).
- Afternoon: product-ops combine and rank proposals. Prepare a short write-up for exec checkpoint.

Day 3 — exec checkpoint and refinement
- 11:00 Exec checkpoint (45m): present top 6 proposals and recommended moves. Execs provide green/yellow/red on each.
- Post-checkpoint: owners incorporate exec feedback and re-score.

Day 4 — final alignment + comms draft
- Morning: drafting all-hands 20-min roadmap slide. Key asks: 3 things to celebrate, 3 priorities, 2 risks + mitigations, 1 cross-org ask of engineers.
- Afternoon: finalize OKR candidates, owners, and measurement signals.

Day 5 — dry run + publish
- Morning: 60m dry run with execs and comms. Final editorial pass.
- 17:00 Publish: OKR candidate list (Confluence), decision ledger (GitHub decisions), all-hands run-of-show and slides (shared drive).

Decision criteria (operationalized)
- Impact > 3 and Cost delta <= 0: prioritize for immediate execution.
- High-impact, high-cost: schedule for a dedicated roadmap sprint and require capacity pledge (ops).
- High risk (ramp risk >=4): include mitigations and fallbacks before roll-out.

Sample deliverables (templates inline)
1) Priority row format (spreadsheet columns): id | title | owner | team | short description | impact | reach | cost_delta | ramp_risk | exec_flag | status | due
2) Decision ledger entry (one line): id | decision | date | owners | rationale | fallbacks
3) All-hands 20m outline: 3m CEO intro, 7m product highlights, 6m ops/infra update (latency/cost wins + risks), 4m closing (what we need from everyone).

Current candidates pulled from backlogs (raw notes)
- Reduce hosted API cold-starts by shipping prefix cache persistence (owner: Priya Kaur, impact 4, cost_delta +1, ramp_risk 3) — Jira PRD-879.
- Dedicated autoscale policy change to increase burst headroom (owner: Arjun Patel, impact 3, cost_delta +2, ramp_risk 2) — OPS-4123.
- Private deployments: add KMS integration checklist for SOC 2 readiness (owner: Clara Gomez, impact 2, cost_delta 0, ramp_risk 1).
- Optimize batching defaults for medium-length prompts (impact 4, cost_delta -2, ramp_risk 3) — cross-team spike needed (eng-serving-runtime + applied-ml).

Risks & mitigation register (short)
- Risk: Q2 Dedicated capacity sales commitments require predictable latency guarantees; infra changes in-flight may decrease headroom. Mitigation: postpone nonessential infra injects; increase monitoring retention; engineering pager coverage for first 72 hours post-change.
- Risk: All-hands messaging leak or premature feature announcement. Mitigation: lock slides to Exec + Comms; embargo policy reminder in Slack (#exec-announce).

Unresolved questions (for the exec checkpoint)
- Which ticket class mandates SLA extension requests vs. product-level responses? (need Exec guidance on trade-offs).
- If we accept +2 cost_delta for Dedicated autoscale, what revenue commitment threshold triggers that as acceptable? (Finance input needed).

Immediate next steps (for this doc owner)
- By EOD today: confirm 5 backlog slices from each team and add owners to the spreadsheet.
- Monday 08:30 PT: post kickoff invite with clear pre-reads (link Confluence page and the short 1-pager).
- Maya: assemble the slide skeleton for All-hands and tag Ops/Comms for content.

Notes to self / scratchpad
- Keep the all-hands ask to a single sentence actionable ask (e.g., "engineers: prioritize two infra low-latency tickets in sprint 16").
- Consider a short internal A/B test message for the all-hands to surface developer-friendly metrics (ops cost per 1M tokens).
- Slack thread to watch: #prod-prioritization (Pin the final ranked list there).

Appendix: useful links and pointers
- Confluence: Company-Q2-Planning-3652 (OKR draft)
- Jira: OPS-4123, PRD-879 (proposals referenced)
- GitHub decisions repo: repo/redwood-inference/decisions/88
- Slack: #leadership-sync, #prod-prioritization

End of playbook.

Document history
- 2026-03-08 Maya Thompson — initial draft and timeline
- 2026-03-10 Arjun Patel — added capacity heatmap note and Dedicated autoscale candidate
- 2026-03-12 Clara Gomez — refined all-hands run-of-show and exec checkpoint prompts
